extracted.intended_audience: policy-makers, regulators, legal scholars, and public broadcasting administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of statutory, regulatory and governance standards that public broadcasters (NHK, SABC, BBC and similar) must meet — covering advertising/sponsorship limits, programming and editorial obligations, governance/appointment rules, regulatory oversight, archiving and financing. Useful for designing, evaluating or comparing public-broadcaster rules and compliance regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements of certain products are forbidden; advertisements must be clearly recognisable and interruptions of regular programmes are restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decree of 27 March 1992 (Articles 8,9,14-16): advertisements of tobacco, alcohol, books, cinema and the press are forbidden except in overseas departments and territories; interruptions permitted only where this will not harm the integrity and value of the programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsorship is financing of television programmes by a sponsor to promote brand/image/name/activities; sponsorship must not contain specific promotional references nor encourage viewers to purchase the sponsor’s products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship must be clearly identified; certain companies (e.g., vending alcoholic drinks, tobacco, prescription drugs) may not sponsor programmes (Articles 17–19). Non-news programmes may be sponsored only where they correspond to educational, social and cultural missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political impartiality and accuracy in news
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters shall be politically impartial and accurate as regards news and present controversial matters from a variety of viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement (Broadcast Law Article 3-2): controversial matters must be presented from a variety of viewpoints; broadcasters required to ensure impartial and accurate news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming diversity obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters must provide a variety of programming, including cultural, educational, news and entertainment material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mandate to cover multiple genres and to balance programming types (e.g., NHK General TV breakdown: news/education/culture/entertainment percentages as an example). Applies to national and regional services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible, broadcasters should provide sound messages to help blind persons understand television programmes, and visual images to assist deaf persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express statutory guidance (Article 3-2) to make programming accessible to disabled audiences; used as a standard for production and technical arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to establish and publish broadcasting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters are required to establish, and make public, broadcasting standards applicable to each type of programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal requirement (Article 3-3): broadcasters must publish standards per programme type and follow them; consultative bodies must be involved in their development (see Consultative Organization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster broadcasting duty
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a disaster, broadcasters must conduct programming so as to minimise the harmful effect of the disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory duty (Article 6-2): programming obligations during emergencies include responsiveness and minimising harm — e.g., NHK’s role in rapid disaster response on Radio 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-service mission and quality standard (NHK general purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide abundant, high-quality domestic programming for the public welfare, receivable nationwide, and conduct international broadcasting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 7: aims include high-quality domestic programming, nationwide reception, and international services — used as a benchmark for content quantity/quality and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary public-service obligations (cultural/educational/local/international)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional obligations include satisfying wishes of the people, enhancing the level of civilisation, providing local and national programmes, popularising modern civilisation, preserving excellent features from the past, and for international services, promoting international friendship and understanding of national culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 44: elaborates specific cultural/educational/local/international aims that shape commissioning, scheduling and editorial choices for public-service broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from interference; editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A form of independence is established: no one may interfere with or regulate broadcast programmes except as provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3 (and parallel provisions): statutory protection to safeguard editorial independence from arbitrary interference; governance and dismissal rules are designed to uphold this independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board (Governors) decides on management, policy and important matters including budget, broadcasting standards and remuneration, and appoints senior officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14 (NHK example): Board must set strategic direction, approve budgets and broadcasting standards; delineates governance accountability and oversight functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and limits on appointment of governors/directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Governors (or board members) must be capable of making fair judgments, have wide experience/knowledge in relevant fields, include regional representation, and must not have disqualifying convictions or recent dismissals; political-party representation limits apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 16 et seq.: appointment qualifications, district representation (at least one from each listed district), and limits (e.g., no more than 4 Governors from any one political party) to protect pluralism and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of tenure and limited dismissal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Governors may only be dismissed on limited grounds (inability to perform, acting contrary to official obligations, malfeasance); outside those grounds they are protected from dismissal against their will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 19–21: job security provisions intended to insulate governors from political pressure; removal procedures must follow statutory grounds and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive and governance roles; officer appointment/dismissal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Directors and officers (President, Vice-President, Directors, auditors) have defined roles: Board sets policy, Directors deliberate on execution; Governors appoint President and auditors; dismissal powers are circumscribed and shared among bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 24–29: allocation of representation and dismissal authorities (e.g., Governors can dismiss President/auditors; President can dismiss Vice-President/Directors with Governors’ consent) — used to evaluate governance arrangements and checks-and-balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and use of Consultative Organization on Broadcast Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: All broadcasters are required to establish a Consultative Organization to oversee quality/service; it must be consulted on development/amendment of broadcast standards and the broadcaster must take its comments into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3-4: broadcasters must provide the advisory body with information (including how comments were considered); this institutionalizes public/advisory oversight of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK central and regional advisory bodies and public listening polls
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK must establish a central advisory body and regional bodies to monitor programming; members nominated by President with Board consent; NHK must conduct regular scientific listening polls and make them public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 44-2 & Article 9(6): formal advisory structures and public polling serve as accountability and audience-feedback mechanisms; nominations require Board consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply and correction; archiving requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of reply for anyone affected by broadcasting of untrue matter (claimable within three months) and an obligation to correct discovered incorrect material; broadcasters must archive broadcast material for three months to give effect to this right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 4–5: procedural standards for accuracy/accountability; archiving supports verification and redress processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial consent and specific ministerial powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions by a public broadcaster require prior ministerial approval (e.g., issuing bonds, transfer/lease of equipment, abolishing/suspending stations beyond specified limits); Minister may order certain broadcasts or research subject to state bearing cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 33–35, 42–47: outlines scope of executive oversight vs. operational independence; used to judge limits on autonomy and required external approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit and advertising prohibitions (NHK financing regime)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK is prohibited from making a profit and from broadcasting commercial advertisements; funding is principally via mandatory receiving fees on equipment capable of receiving NHK broadcasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 9(4), 46, 32: financing model enforces non-commercial public-service funding (e.g., in 1999 nearly 98% income from receiving fees). This is a criterion for financing independence and public funding sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate form and separation of public/commercial operations (SABC)
rubrics_metrics.description: SABC is established as a limited liability company with share capital, formally divided (or to be divided) into public service and commercial operations under a single corporate structure, with public-service operations subject to special statutory obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1999 Act Sections 1, 7, 9: legal form and mandated distinction between public and commercial services determines permitted activities, cross-subsidy rules and regulatory treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: SABC public-service objectives and statutory obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make services available throughout territory on a free-to-air basis; provide programming that informs, educates and entertains; maintain libraries/archives; collect news; conduct R&D; nurture talent and train production staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8 and related provisions: these operational objectives set content, outreach and institutional responsibilities for public-service functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, diversity and editorial standards for SABC public service
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service must make services available in all official languages; reflect unity and cultural/multilingual diversity; enrich cultural heritage; be high quality in all languages; provide significant news/public affairs meeting highest journalism standards — fair, impartial, balanced and independent from government/commercial interests; provide educational, minority sports and targeted services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 10: comprehensive content and inclusion benchmarks (audience language coverage, editorial independence and quality standards) used to evaluate service performance and commissioning priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition, appointment transparency and conflict-of-interest rules (SABC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of 12 non-executive members plus key executives; appointments by President on advice of National Assembly after public shortlist publication to ensure transparency; members must have suitable qualifications and represent cross-section of population; strict conflict-of-interest rules and removal after due inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 12–17: institutional design to ensure representative, qualified oversight and procedures for recusal/removal to preserve integrity and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory oversight mechanisms and statutory codes (IBA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters must comply with a statutory Code of Conduct (e.g., addressing obscenity, violence, accuracy, impartiality) enforced by an independent regulator (IBA); licensing and compliance monitoring powers are vested in the regulator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1993 IBA Act and 1999 Act references: gives regulator power to license, enforce codes and ensure broadcasters adhere to standards; used to assess external accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financing mixes and cross-subsidy mandates (SABC)
rubrics_metrics.description: SABC may fund activities through advertisements, subscription, sponsorship, licence fees or other means; commercial services are mandated to subsidise public services; licence fee provisions exist but may be minor relative to advertising revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8(g), Section 11(d), Section 27: financing structure defines incentives and risks to editorial independence; empirical notes: license fee contributed ~13.5% in 1999, advertising ~76.5%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal Charter and Licence Agreement as governance instruments (BBC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC’s public-service obligations and governance are set out in a Royal Charter and a Licence Agreement between the Secretary of State and the Board of Governors; the Agreement specifies programming standards and accountability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter/Agreement (1996): periodic renewal of charter, Agreement may be approved by House of Commons resolution; these instruments set formal obligations and modes of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for external review and public consultation (BBC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must remain under constant and effective review from outside (public meetings, seminars) and any material changes to programming services must be preceded by an appropriate process of public consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter Article 6 and Agreement Clause 4.3: institutionalised public consultation and external scrutiny as part of governance and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: High general standards and limits on content (BBC Home Services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Home Services shall respect high general standards regarding content, quality and editorial integrity; must be balanced, serve tastes/needs of different audiences, not improperly exploit susceptibilities, not contain abusive treatment of religious views, not offend good taste/decency or public feeling, and not be likely to incite crime or lead to disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clauses 3 and 5: specific content constraints and expectations used to adjudicate complaints and set editorial codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and impartiality on controversial subjects; limits on corporate expression on public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Controversial subjects should be treated with due accuracy and impartiality and, except limited exceptions, services should not contain material expressing the opinion of the Corporation on current affairs or matters of public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clause 5: basis for impartiality codes and editorial guidance; BBC must draw up a code illustrating how to observe these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligatory code and guidance on impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The broadcaster must draw up a code giving guidance as to how content requirements (particularly impartiality) may be observed in services and programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement requirement: the code operationalises statutory and contractual standards into editorial practice and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent complaints body and enforcement (Broadcasting Standards Commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent commission must draw up codes on unjust/unfair treatment, privacy, taste/decency, portrayal of violence/sexual conduct, monitor programmes, publish findings, adjudicate complaints and can order publication of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasting Act 1996 (BSC): mechanisms for complaint resolution and sanctions; empirical data: complaint volumes and upholding rates are tracked (e.g., 685 complaints, 78 upheld in a year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific content duties for Home Services (arts/news/education/children/locality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties include stimulating the arts and cultural activity, providing comprehensive, authoritative and impartial news/current affairs, wide-ranging sports coverage, educational programmes (including original children’s programmes), reflecting audience lives/concerns, and providing reasonable proportion of local programmes for national audiences in devolved nations and regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clause 3 and related clauses: operational content mandates shaping commissioning, scheduling and investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary proceedings broadcasting duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The broadcaster must transmit daily an impartial account of the proceedings in both Houses of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clause 3: ensures parliamentary transparency and the broadcaster’s role in democratic accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: World Service editorial objectives and partnership with foreign office (BBC World Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: World Service must maintain high editorial integrity and quality, and in agreement with the Foreign and Commonwealth Office publish long-term objectives including accurate, unbiased, independent news reporting and a ‘balanced British view’ of developments and representation of British life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clause 9.4: defines international broadcasting remit and relationship with government departments on objectives and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive and public-access obligations; R&D duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The broadcaster is required to establish and maintain an archive with a representative selection of programmes and make reasonable arrangements for public access; must maintain a research and development programme to pursue general objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement Clause 12 and other provisions: archiving and R&D obligations support cultural preservation, public access, and technological innovation planning.
